rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=foe, bilateral_on_top=True, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=12, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-4 param_efficient breast. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-1 (a~0.09,3ep) hr 0.264 BEST; iter-2 (a~0.09,11ep) 0.190; iter-3 (a=0.5,11ep) hr 0.0 DIVERGED -- bilateral gains went NEGATIVE (-0.18,-0.24), train-loss ROSE 7x, PSNR 38->29. So DC-strength is NOT a monotonic lever in the tied-GD prox: too-weak alpha leaves streaks, too-strong overshoots+diverges. The plain GD unroll x=x-alpha*(dc+reg) is step-size-fragile; VN/LPD win by NOT relying on a single hand-tuned step (learned DC depth / primal-dual). (2) FAILURE MODE: under-consistency at safe alpha -- 5 tied steps can't null the sparse-view residual, but a bigger single step diverges. The fix is DEPTH, not step size. (3) ONE KNOB: n_iter 5 -> 12 (deeper weight-TIED DC unroll), alpha reverted to 0.1 (iter-3's 0.5 diverged). All else byte-for-byte iter-2. WEIGHT-TIED => ZERO extra params (VN's free-depth trick). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 12 tied safe-alpha DC steps drive Rx->g much further than 5, removing streaks that 5 steps left, WITHOUT the per-step overshoot that killed iter-3 -> hr rises past 0.264, because on sparse-view CONSISTENCY DEPTH (not step size, not reg cleverness) is the lever. (5) BUDGET: K=12 is ~2.4x the fwd/back-proj of K=5; with train_n=200/bs4 + checkpointing + the 1080s wall backstop, expect ~5-6 epochs (fewer than iter-2's 11 but the anneal still progresses); 200-val pass fits. ~<20min (backstop guarantees it). (6) SERIAL; iter-5 self-dispatches (next: projection-domain filter ON, sparse-view-native, if depth alone plateaus).
